input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 grants termination only for material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and Vendor security/service-level/legal/IP failures (9.3), with a force-majeure exit in 27.3. Nothing anywhere gives Customer a right to terminate for convenience, and Section 2.1 affirmatively denies termination rights across a three-year take-or-pay commitment, so the rule's clause is absent in a term longer than 12 months. Vendor has no convenience right today, and Section 10.2 already refunds prepaid recurring Fees for the post-termination period, so the shortest cure is a new 9.4 giving us a 30-day convenience exit and confirming Vendor has none, plus a conforming edit to 2.1 (retaining the no-reduction restriction) so the take-or-pay clause no longer contradicts the new right.

proposal.summary: Add Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice; bar Vendor convenience termination; conform take-or-pay clause
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a 30-day convenience exit for us and confirmed Vendor has no convenience termination right during a committed term, consistent with our termination playbook; Section 10.2 already refunds prepaid Fees for the post-termination period. We also conformed the take-or-pay commitment so it no longer denies that termination right, leaving the no-reduction restriction intact.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Vendor may not terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

ops.newText: without reduction rights, subject to Section 9.4
